questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the domain of a function from its rule
questions.stem: Ticket #101: A function maps employee IDs to annual salaries; which statement about its domain is correct?

options.text: The domain is the set of employee IDs that actually map to a salary value.
The domain is the set of all possible salary values produced.
The domain includes every real number by default.
The domain is always equal to the codomain.

questions.explanation: The domain contains inputs that the function accepts, not outputs. Salaries form the range, and only valid IDs are inputs.
questions.hint: Domain means inputs, range means outputs.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Recognize when a function has an inverse
questions.stem: Ticket #106: Which condition guarantees that a function possesses an inverse that is also a function?

options.text: The function is defined for all real numbers.
The function has a y-intercept of zero.
The function is one-to-one on its domain.

questions.explanation: An inverse is a function only when each output comes from exactly one input, i.e. one-to-one. Monotonic increasing is one way but not required.
questions.hint: Inverse needs unique inputs per output.
